import pandas as pd
from datetime import timedelta

def run(inputs: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> dict[str, pd.DataFrame]:
    target_snapshot = inputs["target_snapshot"].copy()
    cdc_events = inputs["cdc_events"].copy()
    watermark = inputs["watermark"].copy()
    
    # Get the high_ts watermark value
    high_ts = watermark["high_ts"].iloc[0]
    
    # Filter events that haven't been applied yet (event_ts > high_ts)
    new_events = cdc_events[cdc_events["event_ts"] > high_ts].copy()
    
    # Sort events by user_id, then event_ts, then event_seq for deterministic processing
    new_events = new_events.sort_values(by=["user_id", "event_ts", "event_seq"]).reset_index(drop=True)
    
    # Create a working copy of the snapshot
    snapshot = target_snapshot.copy()
    
    # Build a dict of current state for each user
    user_state = {}
    for _, row in snapshot.iterrows():
        user_id = row["user_id"]
        user_state[user_id] = {
            "email": row["email"],
            "status": row["status"],
            "status_ts": row["status_ts"]
        }
    
    # Process events sequentially per user
    for _, event in new_events.iterrows():
        user_id = event["user_id"]
        event_ts = event["event_ts"]
        op = event["op"]
        email = event["email"]
        
        # Get current state for this user (or initialize if new)
        if user_id not in user_state:
            user_state[user_id] = {
                "email": None,
                "status": None,
                "status_ts": None
            }
        
        current = user_state[user_id]
        
        if op == "D":
            # Soft delete: preserve email from current state if it exists, otherwise use event email
            # Update status to DELETED and status_ts to event_ts
            current["email"] = current.get("email") or email
            current["status"] = "DELETED"
            current["status_ts"] = event_ts
        
        elif op == "U":
            # Update operation
            if current["status"] == "DELETED":
                # User is currently deleted - check resurrection window
                # Resurrection allowed only if event_ts > status_ts + 7 days (strictly greater)
                deletion_ts = current["status_ts"]
                resurrection_threshold = deletion_ts + timedelta(days=7)
                
                if event_ts > resurrection_threshold:
                    # Resurrection allowed
                    current["email"] = email
                    current["status"] = "ACTIVE"
                    current["status_ts"] = event_ts
                # else: resurrection blocked, discard update (do nothing)
            else:
                # User is ACTIVE or new - upsert
                current["email"] = email
                current["status"] = "ACTIVE"
                current["status_ts"] = event_ts
    
    # Build the new snapshot from user_state
    result_rows = []
    for user_id, state in user_state.items():
        # Only include users that have a non-null status (were created or exist)
        if state["status"] is not None:
            result_rows.append({
                "user_id": user_id,
                "email": state["email"],
                "status": state["status"],
                "status_ts": state["status_ts"]
            })
    
    new_snapshot = pd.DataFrame(result_rows)
    
    # Ensure correct dtypes
    if len(new_snapshot) > 0:
        new_snapshot["user_id"] = new_snapshot["user_id"].astype("int64")
        new_snapshot["email"] = new_snapshot["email"].astype("object")
        new_snapshot["status"] = new_snapshot["status"].astype("object")
        new_snapshot["status_ts"] = new_snapshot["status_ts"].astype("datetime64[us]")
    else:
        new_snapshot = pd.DataFrame(columns=["user_id", "email", "status", "status_ts"])
        new_snapshot = new_snapshot.astype({
            "user_id": "int64",
            "email": "object",
            "status": "object",
            "status_ts": "datetime64[us]"
        })
    
    return {"new_snapshot": new_snapshot}
